why: The verse names Timna sister of Lotan, and both records are the sister of Lotan (A only adds the Eliphaz concubine identification of GEN 36:12).
1CH 11:38 'Joel brother of Nathan' stands in the same slot of David's mighty men as 2SA 23:36 'Igal son of Nathan of Zobah', so both records hold the one Nathan of that list.
The verse names Zabad son of Ahlai, which is A; B is the Judahite son of Nathan of 1CH 2:36.

The verse names a Jehoiada 'leader of Aaron' at Hebron; nothing in the text ties him to Benaiah's father (A), though 1CH 27:5 calls that Jehoiada a chief priest, so identity with A is possible but not stated.
A young warrior Zadok in the Aaronite group at Hebron may be Zadok son of Ahitub (A, by tradition) or a separate man (B, though B wrongly calls him Benjamite); the text does not say.
The verse names the father of Jeziel and Pelet who joined David at Ziklag; A's Azmaveth son of Jehoaddah is six generations after Saul (1CH 8:33-36) and cannot be that man.
Elpelet in 14:5 is the earlier of David's two Eliphelets (matching 1CH 3:6), while the later one (14:7, 3:8, 2SA 5:16) is B.
David summons the six chiefs just listed in 15:5-10, so this Joel is the Gershomite chief of 15:7 that A holds, and B is the same man held again.
Both records are the second-degree Levite Benaiah who played the psaltery before the ark.
Both records are the second-degree Levite Benaiah who played psalteries on Alamoth.
The doorkeeper of the ark under David is neither the post-exilic Berechiah son of Asa of 1CH 9:16 nor stated to be Asaph's father; he is a third Berechiah.
Both records are Joel chief of the sons of Gershom at the bringing up of the ark.
Both records are Eliel chief of the sons of Hebron with eighty brethren.
The verse ends 'these were the heads of the fathers of Laadan', so this Shimei belongs to Laadan's house (A), not Gershon's son Shimei whose sons follow in 23:10 (B).
Both records are the Azarel who drew the eleventh lot among the singers.
The verse names the father of Omri, David's officer over Issachar; A is Michael son of Izrahiah, a great-grandson of Issachar (1CH 7:3), whom nothing ties to David's time.
The verse names the father of David's treasurer Azmaveth; A is the priestly ancestor Adiel son of Jahzerah of 1CH 9:12, whom the text never links to him.
The verse names the father of David's storehouse overseer Jehonathan; A is Uzziah son of Uriel in the early Kohathite line of 1CH 6:24, generations earlier.
1CH 3:6 names the first of David's two Eliphelets; the second, in 3:8 and 2SA 5:16, is B.
1CH 4:1 is a descending line (Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, Shobal), so this is Shobal son of Hur, father of Reaiah, which both records hold.
Both records are Shobal father of Reaiah, and A's son of Hur is the same man as B's Shobal listed under Judah.
Both records are Ezer son of Hur, father of Hushah.
This Elkanah follows Korah and Assir, matching Korah's son Elkanah of EXO 6:24 (A), not the later Elkanah son of Joel of 6:36 (B).
Both records are Uriel son of Tahath and father of Uzziah.
The Elkanah whose son is Zophai is Elkanah son of Mahath/Ahimoth (6:35, Ketiv 'Elkanah his son'), which is A, not Amasai's father (B).
Both records are Asaiah son of Haggiah in Merari's line.
The one Elkanah in 6:35 is son of Mahath and father of Zuph (A), while Elkanah son of Joel (B) is in 6:36.
Tahath son of Assir son of Ebiasaph holds the same place as in 6:23-24, and both records are son of Assir.
Both records are Amaziah son of Hilkiah, father of Hashabiah, in Ethan's line.
Both records are Gera son of Bela in this list.
This is the second Gera among Bela's sons (B); A's identification of him with the father of Shimei who cursed David, centuries later, has no support in the text.
1CH 9:10 is the same Jerusalem priests' list as NEH 11:10, where this Jedaiah is son of Joiarib (B), not the Jedaiah family head of EZR 2:36 (A).
Shemaiah's ancestor Hashabiah is son of Bunni in the parallel NEH 11:15 (B); A's son of Amaziah is the much earlier ancestor of David's singer Ethan (1CH 6:45).
The verse names Elkanah grandfather of Berechiah, of the Netophathite villages, which is exactly A.
Both records are the gatekeeper Akkub listed with Shallum, Talmon and Ahiman.
Paul sets this James apart from 'all the apostles', and the only James he names elsewhere is the Lord's brother (GAL 1:19), not the son of Zebedee.
Both records are Ethan the Ezrahite of this verse; A only adds the possible Zerahite identification.
The verse names the father of Kish in Hezekiah's day (B); A is the much earlier Abdi son of Malluch in Ethan's ancestry (1CH 6:44).
Both records are Jeiel of the sons of Elizaphan in this verse (B wrongly calls him Gershonite).
Both records hold the overseer under Conaniah in Hezekiah's reign; A identifies him with Heman's descendant Jehiel of the same reign.
Both records are Shaphan son of Azaliah, Josiah's scribe.
Both records are Shaphan son of Azaliah, Josiah's scribe.
Both records are Shaphan son of Azaliah, Josiah's scribe.
Both records are Shaphan son of Azaliah, Josiah's scribe.
The verse names a chief Levite at Josiah's Passover (B); A is Hashabiah son of Kemuel, David's officer (1CH 27:17).
The verse names a chief Levite at Josiah's Passover (B); A is an overseer under Hezekiah about ninety years earlier (2CH 31:13).
The only Jeroboam the verse names is 'Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin' (A); Jeroboam son of Joash is only the unnamed subject.
Both records are Shaphan son of Azaliah, Josiah's scribe.
Both records are Shaphan son of Azaliah, Josiah's scribe.
Both records are Shaphan son of Azaliah son of Meshullam, Josiah's scribe.
Both records are Shaphan son of Azaliah, Josiah's scribe.
Both records are Shaphan son of Azaliah, Josiah's scribe.
Both records are Elnathan of Jerusalem, father of Nehushta.
The verse names the addressee of 3 John (B); nothing ties him to the Macedonian travelling companion of ACT 19:29 (A).
Both records are the Macedonian Gaius, Paul's travelling companion seized with Aristarchus.
'Herod's praetorium' at Caesarea is the palace built by Herod the Great (B), not Agrippa I (A).
Both records hold Eliezer, priest of the sons of Jeshua, who had married a foreign wife in 10:18.
Both records hold Jarib, priest of the sons of Jeshua, who had married a foreign wife.
The verse names Maaseiah of the sons of Harim (B); A merges him with a different Maaseiah of the sons of Jeshua (10:18).
This Eliezer is listed among the Levites, separate from the priest Eliezer of Jeshua's sons in 10:18 (A), so he is B.
Whether Jehohanan's father Eliashib is the high priest of NEH 3:1 (B) or another man (A) is the long-standing Ezra-Nehemiah dating question, and the text does not settle it.
Both records hold the priestly family head Jedaiah of the house of Jeshua in this list.
'The house of Jeshua' may be the ninth priestly course (A) or the house of the high priest Jeshua son of Jozadak (B); the verse does not say which.
The verse names the Levite family head Jeshua of the sons of Hodaviah whose descendants returned (A), not the later Levite of Nehemiah's day (B).
Both records hold Elam whose 1,254 descendants returned in this list.
Both records are Seraiah son of Azariah and father (ancestor) of Ezra.
Both records hold the Azariah who is father of Amariah-2 and descendant of Meraioth in this shortened high-priestly line.
